turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. I'm... well, I guess I'm here because I just don't care about anything anymore. Like, I used to really love my art classes. But I don't know, the last time I went, the instructor was wearing this really loud perfume, like cheap lavender? It reminded me of my great-aunt's house in Ohio. She always had these little sachets stuffed in her drawers that made all her sweaters smell ancient, and she had this cat that would just stare at you while you ate. 

But anyway, I just stopped going to the classes. I don't even care about our board-game nights anymore. We used to play all the time, but the little wooden pieces always get lost under the rug, and my roommate vacuumed one up once and it made this horrible rattling noise inside the machine for like a week. So I just stopped showing up for that. Or hiking. Or even trying to get back on my soccer team. I just don't care. I basically just sit in my room now while everything slips away. My room gets really cold, actually, because the radiator makes this weird hissing sound if you turn the knob past three, so I just leave it off and sit there.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly states they no longer care about or participate in previously enjoyed activities like art classes, board games, hiking, and soccer.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been feeling this way?

He always kept a glass bowl of those little strawberry candies on it? You know, the ones with the wrappers that look like actual strawberries. I tried to eat one once while he was talking, but it was completely melted to the wrapper. It took me forever just to peel it off, and my fingers got all sticky. I had to use a wet wipe from my purse, but it smelled like fake lemon, and I really hate that smell because it reminds me of the floor cleaner they used in my dorm in college. The janitor would mop at like 6 AM every Tuesday, right outside my door, and the smell would just seep under the crack... 

But anyway, yeah, shortly after the divorce. So I guess it's been about a year and 11 months now of just... feeling like this.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have there been any periods of at least two weeks where your mood was significantly lower or you felt more hopeless than you do on a typical day?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's not really just a two-week thing, it's basically every day. Most days I just wake up with this... this really heavy, hollow feeling right in my chest. It's like there's just no future for me at all beyond my apartment walls. 

Which, by the way, the walls in my bedroom are painted this really awful off-white color. The landlord told me it was 'eggshell' when I moved in, but it actually looks exactly like expired mayonnaise. You know when someone leaves a jar in the fridge way past the date and it gets that weird, translucent yellow crust around the rim? My ex used to do that constantly. He would leave practically empty jars in the fridge for months, just taking up space on the door shelf. And we had this tiny little fridge that would rattle so loudly every time the compressor kicked on. I tried shoving a folded piece of cardboard under the front wheel to level it out and make it stop shaking, but someone spilled juice on the floor and the cardboard just soaked it up and turned into this gross, sticky mush... 

But yeah, I just wake up feeling completely hollow.

turns.doctor_question: In these nearly two years, have there been any stretches of time lasting two months or longer where you felt completely like your old self and didn't have these feelings?
turns.patient_response:
Um, no... I haven't. Not two months. Not even two days, really. It's just been this constant, heavy blur. Two months is a long time... I mean, that's two whole pages on a calendar. 

I actually bought this big wall calendar right around the time the divorce started. It had these really beautiful pictures of lighthouses on it. I found it at this bookstore in the mall that was closing down, and the cashier ringing me up was wearing this incredibly bright orange sweater. It was so bright it almost hurt to look at, like a construction cone. And she was chewing her gum so loudly, just snapping it right in my face while she scanned the barcode. It reminded me exactly of this girl I sat next to in my freshman biology class. She would blow these massive pink bubbles and they would pop and get stuck to her lip gloss. She always wore this really sticky, sparkly lip gloss that smelled like artificial watermelon. 

And one time she accidentally dropped her pen and it rolled all the way down the slanted floor of the lecture hall, right under the professor's podium. He was this really old guy who always wore tweed jackets with those leather patches on the elbows. I always wondered why people put patches there. Like, do elbows really wear through fabric that fast? I guess if you lean on your desk all day... but honestly, my elbows get so dry in the winter anyway, I have to use this special thick oatmeal lotion, and it takes forever to rub in. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about the calendar?

symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits severe tangentiality and loose associations, drifting from the topic of a calendar to a cashier, a former classmate, a professor's jacket, and finally elbow lotion, completely losing track of the original question.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have you experienced any changes in your appetite, such as eating significantly more or less than you usually do?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah... I haven't really been eating much at all. I usually go most of the day without eating anything because, honestly, everything just tastes exactly like cardboard. Which is so weird, because I used to love eating. But now, it's just... I don't know, chalky and bland. 

Like, the other day I tried to make toast, but my toaster is one of those cheap ones where the lever gets stuck halfway down. You have to push it really, really hard to get it to click, and sometimes it pops back up immediately, so you just stand there fighting with it. I bought it at a garage sale from this lady who had maybe fifty ceramic frogs covering her entire lawn. Like, every kind of frog you can imagine—frogs playing the banjo, frogs holding little umbrellas, frogs sitting on lily pads. It was honestly a little unsettling. Her driveway was completely covered in those little spiky balls that fall off sweetgum trees, too. I stepped on one and it went right through the sole of my flip-flop. I was wearing those cheap rubber flip-flops you get at the drugstore for like three dollars, the ones that always blister between your toes if you walk for more than ten minutes. I actually still have a scar on my left foot from wearing a pair of those to an amusement park when I was a teenager. We rode this wooden roller coaster that rattled so violently I thought my teeth were going to fall out, and the guy sitting in front of me lost his baseball cap right on the first drop...

But anyway, yeah, I just don't eat. I've actually noticed my jeans are getting really loose. I've had to start knotting the waistband just to keep them from falling down.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have you ever felt so low that you had thoughts of hurting yourself or that life was not worth living?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah. I guess I have. I just... I keep having these thoughts that I just don't want to wake up anymore. It's like, what's the point? And actually, my friend came over the other day and she found me just sitting there, and I guess I had been saying out loud that I couldn't keep living like this. 

She's the friend who always wears those really clunky wooden clogs. You know the ones? They make this incredibly loud clopping sound on hard floors. We went to a museum once, one of those places with the really high marble ceilings where every sound echoes, and you could hear her walking from like three exhibits away. People kept turning around and staring at us. It was an exhibit on ancient pottery, which was honestly kind of boring. Just rows and rows of brown clay bowls that all looked exactly the same. But there was this one vase that had a tiny little crack down the side, and it made me wonder who broke it. Like, did some ancient person drop it while they were washing it? I drop things in the sink all the time. Just last week I dropped a glass and it shattered into a million tiny pieces, and I had to use a wet paper towel to pick up all the little shards so I wouldn't step on them. I always buy the cheap paper towels because they're on sale, but they never actually absorb anything, they just kind of smear the water around...

But yeah, she found me saying I just didn't want to be here anymore.

turns.doctor_question: Aside from the changes in your appetite, have you noticed that you have much less energy than usual, or that it is difficult to focus on things like reading or watching television?
turns.patient_response:
Um, yeah... I just, I have absolutely no energy. It's like my whole body is made of lead. Even if I've been in bed for half the day, just doing something tiny, like taking a shower or answering one text message, it feels like I've just worked a full shift. 

I used to work shifts at this little diner when I was in college. It had these red vinyl booths that were always sticky, no matter how many times I wiped them down. We had to use this blue spray cleaner that smelled like fake pine needles and ammonia, and it would always make my eyes water. My manager there was this guy named Gary who had the thickest mustache I've ever seen. It completely covered his top lip, like a fuzzy caterpillar just resting under his nose. I always wondered how he ate soup without getting it all over his mustache. Soup is so messy anyway. I tried to eat chicken noodle soup the other day, but the noodles were those really long, slippery ones, and they just kept sliding off the spoon and splashing broth everywhere. I hate when that happens, especially when you're wearing a white shirt. I have this one white t-shirt that I bought at a concert years ago, and it has a tiny little coffee stain right near the hem that I've never been able to get out, no matter how much bleach I use. I even tried that trick where you soak it in white vinegar, but then the shirt just smelled like salad dressing for a week. 

But, um... yeah, I just can't focus on anything. Even watching TV is too much work. I just kind of stare at the wall.
